All three extra references support the boundary rather than contradict it.

single caller chain: _Z11LoadObjects is referenced by exactly one function in the ROM, _ZN5Stage18LoadClsnAndObjects, which is the function immediately below it in address order; nothing outside the span calls either

shared signature: fifteen of the seventeen are _Z-mangled FREE functions (no class component) whose parameter list is identical -- (LVL_Overlay::ObjSubTable&, int, unsigned) -- because LoadObjects calls them all through the one table
left boundary: _ZN3HUDC1Ev ends exactly at 0x020fe190 and is the last function of the HUD class TU (a D1/D0/C1-bearing object, plainly a different translation unit)

right boundary: the four functions at 0x020fea4c..0x020feabc are a dBgCh_Lin group, not part of this TU -- func_ov002_020fea4c and func_ov002_020fea68 copy a Vector3 out of offsets 0x0c and 0x00 of the very struct _ZN8dM3dGLin3SetERK7Vector3S2_ writes at 0x020fea84, and all four are called from one main function at 0x02037624..0x02037788. build/tu_map.json cuts at 0x020fea84 instead; this entry's cut is the corrected one.

source-order corroboration (independent of everything above): mwccarm's section order is the reverse of source order, so the original file's reading order was the reverse of the ROM's addresses. Read that way the file is exactly define-before-use -- fifteen loaders, then the dispatcher, then the public entry point -- and the loaders after LoadSimpleObjects fall in ascending handler-table index 0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14.
boundary_caveats: NOT sinit-corroborated, and that is structural rather than an oversight: this pilot established that ZERO destructor-free TUs exist in any sinit-corroborated module of this ROM (36 corroborated modules, every one of their TUs contains a D1/D0 pair). A TU with no class cannot be constructed by a static initialiser, so the sinit gate has nothing to say about it.
ov002 as a whole is NOT sinit-corroborated (26 sinits vs 79 candidate TUs) and is not in tu_map.json's under-segmented list either.

The membership of _ZN5Stage18LoadClsnAndObjects is the one INFERENCE in this list rather than a fact. It rests on contiguity, on being LoadObjects' only caller, and on the define-before-use reading; it is externally linked, so nothing forces it into this TU the way internal linkage would. The alternative reading is a one-function TU sandwiched between HUD's object and the loader's, which is possible and is not refuted here. Dropping it leaves the other sixteen unchanged.

BLOCKER A -- TOOLING, in principle fixable. To stop the gap object claiming the vtable the TU would have to OWN the .data it lands in. tubuild.splice_tu_entry cannot express that: it hardcodes a single `.text start:.. end:..` line per spliced entry with no path for any other section. The range is already known from boundary_evidence (0x02092660..0x020926c8, the vtable object occupying 0x02092678..0x020926c8), so the claim is knowable; writing it is not currently possible. _ZTV8dScene_c's own 20 words are plausible content -- every slot points at a real ROM function -- so this blocker is about plumbing, not about the bytes.

BLOCKER B -- NAMING, AND IT IS NOT FIXABLE BY ATTRIBUTION AT ALL. This is the important one and it generalises past this TU. The object emits six STB_LOPROC RTTI records that the audit calls HOMELESS -- _ZTI/_ZTS for Scene, ActorDerived and ActorBase -- and no symbols.txt anywhere names them (verified: zero hits across every config/**/symbols.txt; the only matches in config/ are inside this manifest file itself). The reason is that the type-name STRINGS a C++ compiler bakes into _ZTS are the CLASS NAMES, and this tree's names are coinages while the cartridge holds Nintendo's. Measured side by side:

b'8dScene_c\x00' is 7 bytes and b'8dScene_c\x00' is 10, and they are different bytes, so there is no address in the cartridge these three _ZTS records could be attributed to -- their content is not in the ROM and never will be. Since rombuild links -nodead, nothing drops them either, and they would displace bytes inside the module.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WORKSTREAM, stated as a general rule because it is one: NO key-function TU can reach whole-range link-verified while its class name is a project coinage. The vtable is a plumbing problem; the type strings are not. The only fix is renaming the class to the ROM's own name (Scene -> dScene_c, ActorDerived -> dBase_c, ActorBase -> fBase_c, per include/Scene.h reading 4), which is a separate tree-wide change and was not attempted here.

NEW CASE NOT SEEN IN EITHER PRIOR PILOT: _ZN7Vector3D1Ev is also unlicensed. It is types.h's inline `~Vector3(){}`, re-emitted by every TU that destroys a Vector3, and it DOES have a configured ROM home (arm9 0x020072c0) -- confirmed identical body (`bx lr`) and zero inbound relocations within this TU via the same ELF read. Neither policy schema fits it: compiler_only_output refuses any symbol with a configured ROM home (it is not compiler-only), and externalized_output is restricted to _ZTI/_ZTS objects by its own validation, not .text functions. Left unlicensed alongside this TU's own vtable/RTTI; widening one of the two policy schemas (or adding a third) to cover a compiler-duplicated ordinary function is follow-up work, not attempted here. Render()/CleanupResources() were reconciled against the real header before verifying: the generator's local shadow struct pair (Base/Derived, standing in for the real inherited Model member) is gone in favour of `mModel.Render(0)`, matching ShipWater's precedent; and CleanupResources' mMeshCollider access, which the generator wrote as a raw offset cast to `dBgW*`, is now the plain member calls `mMeshCollider.IsEnabled()`/`.Disable()` -- the raw-cast form was ALSO a latent correctness bug once the file-table externs were retyped to `ArrowSignFileColumn`, not just a readability issue: the legacy file's byte-offset pointer arithmetic assumed a `char[]` base type, and multiplying an already-struct-typed pointer by 0xc again overshot every row lookup, which is what verify's first pass caught as a 999-word DIFF.
